findings.ref: T-003.contract.json 'CYCLE-3 REMEDIATION ADDENDUM'; reports/implementation/epic-193-a5-capability-resolver/T-003.md '### Mutation Kills'; tests/resolve-project-context-block-check.py run_t003_case ('evaluate-predicate-schema-error', 'dsl-warn-unsorted-affected-components')
findings.note: The claims carrying this cycle's discriminating power are prose-only. (a) evaluate-predicate-schema-error, the fixture added to close cycle-3 Major #1 (PREDICATE_SCHEMA_ERROR classification decoupled from the hardcoded returncode == 2), is explicitly documented as NOT failing against the pre-fix code -- 'the fixture's own value is architectural ... not a RED-to-GREEN transition for this specific fixture' -- so the RED capture gives it zero coverage, and its entire justification rests on a claimed mutation kill ('reverting the token check to "NOT_THE_REAL_TOKEN" ... 182 passed / 2 failed') for which no log, transcript, or retained artifact appears anywhere in the bundle. (b) dsl-warn-unsorted-affected-components is the SOLE assertion locking step 7's ascending-lexicographic per-component fan-out (sorted(affected_components) in _evaluate_capabilities) -- a property this task's own Requirements line claims as its REQ-005 share -- and its whole discriminating power rests on its stub resolve-component-paths.py (declared sha 9ec08dec...) genuinely returning affected_components in DESCENDING order. That stub and the fixture's capability-registry.json (2f1f0255...) are absent from the bundle, the fixture appears in no RED capture, and no mutation kill is claimed for it; a stub that happened to return them already sorted would leave the expectation ['comp-a','comp-z'] green against an unsorted implementation. Under the no-credit-for-unverifiable-claims rule neither can be counted as verified. Remedy: retain the mutation runs as first-class evidence artifacts (as the RED/GREEN pairs already are) and give the fan-out sort a kill whose evidence is reproducible from the bundle. Note the two prior-cycle findings this pass DID close verifiably: traceability.log now cites ALL_CASE_NAMES line 276 / run_t003_case line 437 / thirteen fixtures / 184-0, all three of which check out exactly against the driver in this bundle; and MANIFEST.sha256, the contract comment, and both Outputs tables now agree on f6bc6796... for the staged resolve-project-context.py.

The co-located sibling-module import is guarded only by 'except ImportError'. A registry_discovery.py that fails to import for any other reason (SyntaxError, or any exception raised at module scope) escapes uncaught, producing a raw Python traceback with no 'capability-resolver:' diagnostic line and no Resolver Evidence -- precisely the failure mode the registry-discovery-unimportable fixture was added to close, and a security-spec B5 (no-local-path-in-committed-output) containment bypass. Widening to 'except Exception' (or at minimum ImportError + SyntaxError) closes the class rather than the single instance.

REQ-004 scopes a severity: 'warn' entry's detail to that node's 'capability_id/component_id/(declaration_index, only for a conditional_facets[].when node)'. _warn_diagnostic_detail interpolates declaration_index unconditionally, rendering the literal 'declaration_index=None' for every trigger-evaluation node. (id, detail) uniqueness under AC-024 is preserved, so this is cosmetic drift, but the three dsl-warn-* fixtures and expected_warn_diagnostic() now pin the drifted form.

The sys.path mutation is never reverted, so it shadows stdlib/site names for the remainder of the process; the driver's own run_draft7_validator_keyword_checks imports this module in-process, so the side effect outlives the call there too. Self-disclosed as record-only in the report's Unresolved Items; repeated for completeness. A try/finally restore closes it.
